svg.text: Konata-style trace: one row per instruction, one column per cycle · derived from rtl/RXVFetch, RXVDecode, RXVLSU, RXVMulExec, RXVTLB, RXVCommitBuffer
A — steady state, multiply, DTLB miss and recovery
no branch mispredicts; both PTE reads hit in the data cache
DTLB miss — hardware page-table walk (2 × PTE read via the D$)
completed out of order — waiting in the ROB
B — LSU hazard kill: a load issued in the shadow of an older miss
the younger load has already left decode when the older one reports busy, so it cannot be stalled — it is killed and replayed
The integer unit has a 1-cycle latency and forwards its result to the
next instruction, so the dependent sub issues without a bubble.
M1–M5 give a 5-cycle result latency, but the next instruction issues
to the integer unit behind it and completes first — out of order.
busy is asserted the cycle after the lookup, so the access is held in
LSU stage 1 while the walker reads two PTEs through the D$ port.
independent work continues under the miss
i5–i7 are not LSU ops: they issue, execute and write back while the
walk runs, then the ROB releases them in order behind the load.
later loads wait, then go back-to-back
lsu_busy blocks LSU dispatch at decode, so i8 is held rather than
killed; afterwards the LSU accepts one load per cycle.
the miss itself is not killed
j0 was already accepted into LSU stage 1 in the cycle before busy
rose, so it is simply replayed once the translation arrives.
exec_valid & lsu_stall raises lsu_busy_kill: the access is dropped
before the cache sees it, and kill_valid clears the two most recent
ROB dispatches and flushes the front end.
lsu_resteer_tgt is the killed load’s own PC; on the second attempt
it is held at decode by lsu_busy and then hits in the DTLB.
held in the LSU (TLB / cache busy)

Cycle counts assume no branch mispredicts and a 4 KB page (two PTE reads). A PTE read that misses in the D$ adds a line fill to the walk; a D$ miss on the load itself stalls the LSU in exactly the same way.
